Why Scanned PDFs Are So Large and How to Shrink Them

Published November 2, 2026 · Ubahin Team

A single scanned page can be over 2 MB, while a hundred-page PDF of plain text may be only a few hundred KB. The difference is what is inside the PDF.

The main cause: pages are images

A scanned PDF stores each page as an image. For example, an A4 sheet scanned at 300 dpi produces an image of about 2480 × 3508 pixels. An image that size makes a big file, especially if it is saved at high quality or in color when the content is just black-and-white text.

How to make it smaller

  1. Lower the resolution or compress the images. For a document that is only read on screen, around 150 dpi is usually clear enough. Try Compress PDF starting at the Medium level.
  2. Shrink photos before turning them into a PDF. If the document is made from phone photos, reduce the photos with Compress Image, then combine them with JPG to PDF.
  3. Remove pages you do not need, including blank pages.

Trade-offs to know about

PDF compression on Ubahin works by re-rendering each page as a JPEG image. For scanned PDFs this is fine, since the content is already an image. For a PDF that contains real text, the result becomes an image, so the text can no longer be copied or searched. If your file is already efficient, the original size is kept.

How small is reasonable?

If the limit is 500 KB for several pages, aim for a result that is still clearly readable. Check the final file by zooming in before you upload it.
